name: Photogravure
summary: A way to etch a photograph into a copper plate. The print has the full range of tones of the photograph, in a rich intaglio ink.
how: Expose a gelatin tissue under a positive; the light hardens the gelatin in proportion to its tone.
Transfer the tissue to a copper plate that has an aquatint grain of about 150 to the inch.
Etch the plate in baths of ferric chloride; the soft gelatin lets the acid bite deeper.
Print on damp paper with a copper-plate press, in a warm black or brown ink.

origin.note: Henry Fox Talbot patented his photographic engraving in 1852.

adoptions.via: Karel Klíč makes the mature Talbot-Klič process, which stays in use.
Alfred Stieglitz prints the plates of Camera Work as photogravures.
